ideas.title: The 3-Price Trap Making You Overspend
ideas.angle: Exposes the classic asymmetric dominance effect (Decoy Effect) used by streaming services and tech giants, challenging viewers with a live choice between three pricing tiers to prove their brain was manipulated. Drives comments as viewers debate whether they fell for option B or C.

hook.en: Stop picking the middle option right now.

ideas.reason: Directly taps Archetype 1 & 2 by giving the viewer a live decision test on screen. The Decoy Effect is proven behavioral economics (MIT / Dan Ariely research) that triggers massive replay rates to verify the trick.
sources: MIT / Dan Ariely - Predictably Irrational (The Economist Pricing Experiment)
Journal of Consumer Research - Asymmetric Dominance in Choice Architecture

ideas.title: Why You Love Discounts But Hate Surcharges
ideas.angle: Reveals the Framing Effect and loss aversion trick where stores charge you identical amounts but frame one as a 'cash discount' instead of a 'card penalty' to bypass your brain's pain receptors. Asks viewers to comment whether they check itemized receipts.

hook.en: Your brain hates penalties, not paying more.

ideas.reason: Uses Archetype 2 (Forbidden Money Secrets) with immediate, visceral relevance to everyday checkout habits. Loss aversion creates high engagement because viewers realize their subconscious pain receptors are being hacked.
sources: Daniel Kahneman & Amos Tversky - Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
Stanford Graduate School of Business - The Psychology of Surcharges vs Discounts

ideas.title: Say These 5 Words to Double Sales
ideas.angle: Breaks down the BYAF ('But You Are Free') psychological compliance technique that instantly disables psychological reactance and doubles conversion rates in negotiations and transactions. Prompts viewers to comment on how they will test this in their next negotiation.

hook.en: Never negotiate without saying these 5 words.

ideas.reason: Delivers Archetype 3 (Social Power & Micro-Behavior Decoding). Meta-analyses of 42 field studies confirm the BYAF technique consistently doubles persuasion rates, delivering instant tactical value that viewers save and share.
sources: Christopher Carpenter - A Meta-Analysis of the 'But You Are Free' Technique (Communication Studies)
Gueguen & Pascual - Evocation of Freedom and Acceptance of a Request
